chunks: My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: Sa'd bin Abdullah told us, that Ahmad bin Muhammad bin 'Isa told us, from al-Hasan bin Ali al-Khazzaz, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) will on the Day of Resurrection hold onto the Waist Cloth of Allah, and we will hold onto the Waist Cloth of our Prophet, and our party will hold onto our Waist Cloth. Then he said: The Waist Cloth is the Light.

key_terms.النُّورُ: The Light, identified as the true nature of the Hujzah
key_terms.حُجْزَة: Waist cloth or loincloth, used here as a metaphor for holding onto authority or light
key_terms.شِيعَتُنَا: Our party/followers, referring to the Shia

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Hujzah' (Waist Cloth) in the context of the Day of Resurrection according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Mani al-Akhbar* illustrates the Shia concept of *Tawassul* and spiritual intercession through a hierarchical chain of holding onto the 'Hujzah' (waist cloth), symbolizing closeness to the Divine. Imam al-Rida clarifies that this 'Hujzah' is not merely physical but represents Divine Light (*Nur*), emphasizing the metaphysical connection between the Ahl al-Bayt and their followers. This structure underscores the unique status of the Shia as those who maintain the strongest link to the Prophet through the Imams on the Day of Judgment.

en.basel-kadem: 9.	My father, may Allah grant him mercy, said: We were told by Sa’d bin Abdullah, that he said: We were told by Ahmad bin Muhammed bin ‘Isa, from Hasan bin Ali al-Khazzaz, from Abu’l-Hasan al-Rida, peace be upon him, that he said:

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, will on the Day of Resurrection grab hold of the Waist Cloth of Allah, and we will grab hold of the Waist Cloth of our Prophet, and our party [1] will grab hold of our Waist Cloth. Then he said: The Waist Cloth is the Light.
